# How to Lock In Lower AI Costs with Reserved Capacity


"Reserved capacity" is how big companies lock in lower AI prices: they promise to use a lot of AI for months, and get a discount in return. Let's be honest up front — that big-company version is bought through cloud consoles and sales teams, not something you click together at home. But the *idea* behind it (commit a little, save a lot) exists in several everyday versions that anyone can use. This guide walks you through those — using only buttons that actually exist.

## Before you start
- An account with at least one AI assistant (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude or Copilot — the free versions are fine)
- Rough time: **10 minutes**
- No credit card needed for Steps 1–3
- Honesty note: prices and plan names change often — always check the tool's own pricing page before you pay for anything

---

## Step 1 — Work out what you're paying now
Before saving money, see where it goes. List every AI subscription you have — many people quietly pay for two tools that do the same job. Check your bank statement or your phone's subscription list for names like ChatGPT Plus, Gemini, Claude Pro or Copilot Pro.

💬 Example:
```text
My AI spending:
- ChatGPT Plus: $20/month  (use it daily)
- Another assistant: $20/month  (opened twice last month → cancel candidate)
```
You'll know it worked when you can say in one sentence how much you pay per month, and for what.

---

## Step 2 — Get the most out of free versions before paying
The free tiers of ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Meta AI handle most everyday tasks: summarizing, drafting emails, meal plans, translations. The cheapest AI is the one you don't pay for. Only upgrade on the day you actually run into a limit that bothers you.

💬 Example:
```text
Try this in the FREE version of any assistant first:
"Summarise this email thread in 5 bullet points."
```
You'll know it worked when a whole week passes and you haven't hit a paywall for your daily tasks.

---

## Step 3 — Switch to the lighter model for everyday jobs
Most assistants offer a fast, light model and a slower, premium one — and the light one is enough for simple tasks. Look for the model name at the top of the chat window and tap it: in Gemini the light option is called **Flash**, at Claude it's **Haiku**, at ChatGPT the names with **mini** in them. On paid plans, premium models often have usage caps — using the light model saves that quota for when it matters.

💬 Example:
```text
Shopping list, quick email, short summary  → light model (Flash / Haiku / mini)
Contract analysis, tricky planning          → premium model
```
You'll know it worked when answers arrive noticeably faster and your premium-model allowance stops running out.

---

## Step 4 — Pay yearly instead of monthly (where it's offered)
Here's the closest everyday cousin of "reserved capacity": several AI tools give you roughly two months free if you pay for a year up front. For example, Claude Pro and Perplexity Pro both offer discounted annual billing. Open the tool's billing or subscription page and look for a monthly/yearly switch. Golden rule: only prepay a year for the ONE tool you've already used daily for at least a month.

💬 Example:
```text
Monthly plan:  $20 × 12 = $240 a year
Annual plan:   ~$200 a year  → about 2 months free
```
You'll know it worked when the billing page shows your next renewal a year away — at a lower total than 12 monthly payments.

---

## Step 5 — For tinkerers: prepaid credit with a spending cap
If you use AI through an API key (for a hobby project or a small automation), don't leave billing open-ended. OpenAI's API billing, for example, works with prepaid credit — you top up a fixed amount and it simply can't overspend. Most platforms also let you set usage limits or email alerts; Google Cloud has budget alerts for the same job.

💬 Example:
```text
Top up: $10 prepaid  (hard ceiling — can't be exceeded)
Email alert at: $5
```
You'll know it worked when a test question costs a fraction of a cent and the alert email arrives at your set level.

---

## Step 6 — For tinkerers: batch processing is a genuine 50% off
This is the one real "half price" button in the AI world. If you don't need answers instantly, both OpenAI and Anthropic run **batch** jobs at 50% below the normal API price — you submit a pile of tasks, and the answers arrive within 24 hours. Perfect for anything that can wait overnight.

💬 Example:
```text
Great for batch:  "Categorise these 500 product reviews by tomorrow morning."
Not for batch:    a live conversation with a customer.
```
You'll know it worked when the job shows up on your usage page at the discounted batch rate.

---

## So what's the "reserved capacity" that companies buy?
It's the corporate version of the same idea, at cloud scale: a company commits to months of heavy AI usage and in return gets guaranteed speed and lower unit prices. Several providers offer it — Amazon (Provisioned Throughput on AWS Bedrock), Google (Provisioned Throughput on Vertex AI), and OpenAI and Anthropic through their enterprise and priority tiers. It's set up through cloud consoles or sales teams and involves real financial commitment. If your workplace uses a lot of AI, it's a great question for your IT team — but it's not something to buy from your sofa, and no honest guide should tell you otherwise.

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake:** Paying for a premium plan "just in case."
  **Fix:** Start free and upgrade the day you actually hit a limit — not before.

- **Mistake:** Buying an annual plan for a tool you might abandon.
  **Fix:** Only prepay a year after a month of genuine daily use.

- **Mistake:** Assuming "up to 50% off" applies to chat subscriptions.
  **Fix:** The real 50% belongs to batch API pricing; chat plans like ChatGPT Plus are flat monthly fees.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Steps 1–4 are for you. Most households can halve their AI spending just by canceling a duplicate subscription and switching to yearly billing on the tool they truly use.

- **For your business or work:** Steps 5–6 add up fast: batch processing alone halves the cost of any AI task that can wait overnight. And if your company's AI bill is serious, ask IT about reserved capacity — that's exactly who it's for.

- **If you're just getting started:** Stay on free versions (Step 2) and learn the light-vs-premium model switch (Step 3). You can get months of real value before spending a single dollar.

## Try it now
Open your AI assistant, tap the model name at the top of the chat, and switch today's simple questions to the light model. That one habit alone stretches a paid plan — or keeps you comfortably inside the free tier.
